newsitem.title: USA: Quaker declines comment on Snapple rumor.
newsitem.headline: Quaker declines comment on Snapple rumor.

text.p: Quaker Oats Co declined to comment Monday on rumors reported by the media that it might sell its Snapple beverage division.
"Our policy is not to comment on rumors," Mark Dollins, spokesman for Chicago-based Quaker Oats, said.
Quaker has said previously that it expects an operating loss this year for Snapple, which it acquired two years ago for $1.7 billion. However, the loss is expected to be less than a year ago.
Quaker recently outlined its distribution strategy for Snapple, adding it will remain a national brand.
Operating losses from Snapple, which Quaker Oats has called disappointing, have fueled speculation in the past about the fate of the fruit-flavored and iced tea beverage company.
In a recent filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, Quaker said it was reviewing Snapple to see if it would have to take a charge to reduce the carrying value of the business.
